narrative:
The model has analyzed your academic journey and determined that there’s a **14% chance** you might not pass your final year. While this isn’t a certainty, it’s high enough that your school has decided you should take extra remedial courses to help you succeed. Think of it like a warning light on a dashboard—it’s not saying disaster is inevitable, but it’s urging you to pay attention and take action before things get harder.

The decision isn’t based on random guesswork. Instead, it looks at three key factors that stand out in your situation compared to most students who aren’t in this position. The first is your **history of past academic challenges**. Unlike many students who’ve never failed a class before, your record is clean—but the model is also considering how other students with similar backgrounds have performed. While this factor *actually works in your favor* (since you haven’t struggled before), it’s still a reminder that consistency matters.

The second big influence is your **mother’s level of education**. Most students whose mothers have completed higher education tend to do better, but your mother’s education level is lower than average for students who pass without extra help. This doesn’t mean your mother’s education is the reason you might struggle—it’s more about how these patterns have played out in the past for other students. The model is flagging this as a factor to watch closely.

Finally, your **aspirations for the future** play a role. Almost all students who pass without extra support say they want higher education, and your goal aligns with theirs. This is a positive sign, but the model is treating it as a reminder that big ambitions require extra effort to stay on track.

Here’s what you should do next: **focus on the areas where the model sees potential risks**. Since your study time is already on the lower end compared to peers who pass easily, consider adding even more dedicated study hours. Your family’s support is a strength—lean on them to help you stay organized. And while your health is currently a concern, addressing that will make everything else easier. The remedial courses aren’t a punishment; they’re a chance to reinforce what you’re learning and build confidence before the final year. Use this as an opportunity to turn the warning into a success story.
